hsr_roughing.description: SolidCAM HSR adaptive roughing — hybrid waterline + offset with trochoidal motion in tight corners. Constant cutter engagement, smooth feed, ideal for hard milling.

clearance_z.description: Safe Z above stock for rapids

trochoidal_in_corners.description: Use trochoidal motion in narrow corners

rapid_z_clearance_mm.description: Z lift for transitions within stock

min_link_length_mm.description: Min length for cutting motion (else lift)

hsr_rest_roughing.description: Re-rough after a larger tool. Targets material left in corners and detail areas. Uses stock-aware adaptive engagement to clear unmachined regions only.

min_rest_thickness_mm.description: Skip rest areas thinner than this

expand_rest_area_mm.description: Overlap into machined area for blending

extend_to_full_depth.description: Extend each rest pass to part bottom

trochoidal_in_corners.description: Trochoidal motion in narrow rest pockets

hss_constant_z.description: Z-level waterline finishing for steep walls. Constant axial step, follows part contour at each Z. Best for vertical / near-vertical surfaces.

steep_area_only.description: Limit to steep regions (use combined for shallow)

spiral_between_levels.description: Spiral down vs lift between Z levels

hss_linear.description: Parallel pass surface finish. Best for shallow / horizontal regions. User-defined cut direction angle. Constant XY step, projected onto surface.

hss_radial.description: Radial pass finish from a center point. Best for circular bosses, hemispheres, and rotational features. Step-over varies with radius.

hss_spiral.description: Continuous spiral toolpath finish. No stepovers / no air-cut transitions. Excellent for hemispheres and round bosses with no chatter from re-entry.

hss_3d_stepover.description: Constant scallop height across all surface angles. Step-over auto-adjusts on slopes to maintain uniform finish quality. Best for organic surfaces.

hss_pencil_trace.description: Single-pass cleanup along inside corners and concave fillets. Tool tracks the natural corner contour. Best after a finish pass left scallops in fillets.

hss_boundary.description: Offset toolpath following user-defined boundary curves. Constant offset onto the surface. Useful for trim edges and sealing surfaces.

hss_morph.description: Smooth morphing toolpath between two user-defined boundary curves. Useful for blending transitions, sweeping rib surfaces, and freeform finishing.

hss_combined_finish.description: Hybrid finish that auto-routes steep regions to constant-Z waterline and shallow regions to 3D step-over, blended seamlessly. One-op solution for full part finish.

hss_rest_finish.description: Finish residual material left by a previous larger finishing tool (typically in fillets/corners). Stock-aware step-over keeps engagement constant.

hss_3d_corner.description: Single-pass 3D corner trace using bi-tangent contact. Tool stays tangent to both intersecting surfaces along internal corner curve. Best for hard-milled mold cores.

key_concepts: Constant-Z waterline excels on steep walls (>30deg) — depth-of-cut perpendicular to surface stays bounded.
3D step-over / linear excels on shallow regions (<30deg) — XY step controls scallop directly.
Combined finish auto-blends both based on a transition angle (typically 30-45deg).
Use overlap_angle_deg to avoid an unmachined seam where the methods meet.
best_practices: Default transition_angle_deg to 30deg for general parts, 45deg for steep-wall-dominated molds.
If using two separate ops (constant-Z + linear), set steep_area_only and shallow_area_only with matching cutoff angles plus 5deg overlap.
Always inspect the steep/shallow boundary on the first part — re-tune to eliminate witness marks.

training_topics.topic: Scallop Height as the Universal Quality Metric
key_concepts: Scallop = h = R - sqrt(R^2 - (s/2)^2) where R is ball-end tool radius and s is step-over.
Step-over s = 2 * sqrt(2*R*h - h^2) — pre-compute target step from desired finish.
constant_scallop step-over modes auto-adjust XY step on slopes to keep h constant.
Typical targets: 0.005 mm (mirror), 0.010 mm (mold finish), 0.025 mm (general), 0.050 mm (rough finish).
best_practices: Use scallop_height_mm in HSS strategies instead of fixed step_over_mm whenever the surface has varying slope.
For hand-polished molds target 0.005 mm scallop (saves ~30% polish time vs 0.010 mm).
Cap with max_step_over_mm to avoid unnecessarily fine spacing on near-flat regions.

key_concepts: Trochoidal looping replaces full-engagement plunges with circular cycloid motion that maintains a target max_engagement_pct.
Activated automatically in narrow corners / slots where straight pass would exceed engagement target.
trochoidal_loop_radius_mm should be 1.5-2.0x tool radius for stable chip evacuation.
Reduces peak cutting force by 50-70% vs full-slot plunge — extends tool life dramatically in hard materials.
best_practices: For Aluminum / 6061, set max_engagement_pct = 60-80% (HSR can take heavy engagement on soft materials).
Always enable trochoidal_in_corners on adaptive HSR — straight plunge in tight corners breaks tools.

key_concepts: smoothing_radius_mm rounds sharp corner transitions in the toolpath — smaller value = more accurate, larger = less servo strain.
min_segment_length_mm filters out micro-segments that overwhelm controller look-ahead buffers (Heidenhain TNC: 0.05-0.1 mm typical).
max_acceleration_g caps post-processed feed rate when path curvature would exceed machine capability — prevents servo lag.
fillet_corners replaces zero-radius vertices with the smoothing_radius — controllers handle this much better.
best_practices: Match smoothing_radius_mm to controller tolerance: Fanuc AICC = 0.01 mm, Heidenhain SmuRF = 0.05 mm, Siemens Compressor = 0.02 mm.
On 5-axis machines limit max_acceleration_g to 0.3-0.5 (preserves rotary axis dynamic accuracy).
If you see motion 'choking' on the machine, increase min_segment_length_mm before reducing feed.

key_concepts: rest_source 'previous_tool' uses the previous tool geometry to compute rest mathematically (fast, deterministic).
rest_source 'stock_model' uses the actual updated stock model (slower, but accurate when previous ops left scallops).
Set rest_source = 'both' to take the union — safest for finish, slowest to compute.
min_rest_thickness_mm filters microscopic rest areas that aren't worth machining (0.02-0.10 mm typical).
best_practices: Always sequence: large rougher → smaller rougher (rest) → finishing tool (rest finish) — three-stage rest hierarchy.
On molds, do a hand-pencil-trace pass after rest finish — picks up corners both methods miss.
Set expand_rest_area_mm = 0.2-0.5 mm so rest passes overlap previous machining (no witness lines).

key_concepts: Pencil trace projects the corner curve onto the surface — simple but can miss curved fillet bottoms.
Bi-tangent (3D corner cleanup) computes the true tangent contact between tool and both surfaces — exact corner finish.
Bi-tangent requires the corner to be larger than tool radius (else use a smaller tool).
use_3d_offset = true uses true 3D offset surface (slower, more accurate than projected).
best_practices: For mold cores with internal fillets > tool radius: use HSS 3D Corner Cleanup with use_3d_offset=true.
For sharp corners (< 90deg): use Pencil Trace with multi-pass (2-3 passes_per_corner).
Always verify corner radius vs tool radius before scheduling — undersized tool = bi-tangent fails.
